Simulation-based calibration check for a study design

Source: R/fp_calibrate.R
fp_calibrate.Rd

Simulates many datasets from a design with simulate_fp(), fits one or more false-positive models to each with fp_occu(), and scores how often the credible intervals contain the true values and how biased the posterior means are. Use it before collecting data, to ask whether the correction will be calibrated for the number of sites, occasions, and verified sites you can afford, and whether a constant false-positive rate is enough under the confusion you suspect.

Usage

fp_calibrate(
  design,
  models = list(constant = ~1),
  occ = ~x,
  det = ~1,
  reps = 50,
  prob = 0.95,
  base_seed = 1L,
  parallel = FALSE,
  fit_args = list(chains = 4, parallel_chains = 1, iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling =
    1000, adapt_delta = 0.95)
)

Arguments

design

A data frame (or list) whose columns are arguments of simulate_fp(); each row is one cell of the design. Arguments not given take the defaults of simulate_fp().

models

Named list of formulas for the false-positive rate, one model per element, as in the fp argument of fp_occu(). The default fits only the constant-rate model.

occ, det

Formulas for occupancy and true detection, shared by all models. Simulated data have the occupancy covariate x and the detection covariates bio and aci.

reps

Number of replicate datasets per cell. Each costs one Stan fit per model. Fifty replicates give a Monte Carlo standard error of about 0.03 for a coverage of 0.95.

prob

Width of the credible intervals scored.

base_seed

Integer. Replicate j (counting over cells and replicates) uses seed base_seed + j, so results are reproducible and every model sees exactly the same datasets.

parallel

Logical. Fit replicates in parallel with 'furrr'. Set the plan first, e.g. future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 8), and keep parallel_chains = 1 in fit_args. In interactive sessions with 'progressr' installed, a progress bar shows the estimated time remaining, also when fitting in parallel.

fit_args

List of further arguments for fp_occu(). Unless set here, random_recorder is TRUE only when the design simulates a recorder effect (sd_recorder > 0): fitting one whose true standard deviation is zero produces divergent transitions.

Value

A tibble of class fp_calibration, one row per replicate, model, and scored quantity, with the truth, the posterior mean and interval, whether the interval covered the truth, and sampler diagnostics. Use base::summary() for coverage, its Monte Carlo standard error, bias, and RMSE per cell and model.

Details

The scored quantities are the occupancy intercept and slope (occ_(Intercept), occ_x), the false-positive rate averaged over sites (p10_bar, against the realized mean rate), the detection probability of the verified method (p_verified), and, for models that include the confusing gradient w, its effect on the false-positive rate (fp_w).

See also

fp_verification_curve(), simulate_fp()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
design <- data.frame(p10 = 0.05, conf_effect = c(0, 1.5), conf_cor = 0.7)
cal <- fp_calibrate(design,
                    models = list(constant = ~ 1, fp_on_x = ~ x),
                    occ = ~ x, reps = 50)
summary(cal)
} # }
